displayName: Web Code Stats: HTML, CSS & JS Report
description: Report on a web project: technology stack (React, Vue, Vite, Tailwind, PWA…), observations, HTML pages, assets, and counts of what you choose in HTML, CSS and JavaScript/TypeScript. In English or Spanish.
config.author: Author shown in the report header. Also with the **Web Code Stats: Set report author** command.
config.language.auto: Same as VS Code (Spanish if VS Code is in Spanish, English otherwise).
config.html.metrics: What to count in HTML files (and the markup of `.vue`, `.svelte` and `.astro` components). Empty list = skip HTML.
config.html.tags: Tags counted one by one by the `tags` metric (e.g. `input`, `img`, `a`).
config.css.metrics: What to count in style files (`.css`, `.scss`, `.less` and the `<style>` of components). Empty list = skip CSS.
config.js.metrics: What to count in JavaScript and TypeScript files (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx` and the `<script>` of components). Empty list = skip JavaScript.
config.perFile: Add a table with the values of each file.
config.exclude: Glob of files and folders to leave out.
config.maxFiles: Maximum number of files analysed per language (the inventory looks at up to five times as many).
config.sections: Report sections besides the HTML, CSS and JavaScript metrics.
part.summary: Summary: project type, size and key figures
part.insights: Observations: what is done well and what to review
part.stack: Technology stack: frameworks, build tools, styles, testing, deployment, package.json
part.pwa: Progressive web app: manifest, icons, service worker
part.pages: HTML pages: lang, viewport, title, description, favicon, Open Graph, h1
part.assets: Files and assets: files by type, size and the heaviest ones
